summary: CPU-ONLY cost gate for the suffix+MTP hybrid: replay banked SWE-Verified served token streams against a warmed suffix tree (per-request + global cross-request corpus) and measure, at each accept-event spine tip, the suffix correct-continuation length (expected accepted tokens if a 3-deep suffix tail were grafted) vs the cat9 deep-leaf accepts it would displace, net of the GDN per-node tax. Decides go/no-go for a GPU prototype. NO GPU, NO model, NO docker - pure offline token-stream analysis.

data.perRequestStreams:
Usable per-request streams (REAL, full token-id, SWE/code-agent content, NOT toy):
- Deliverable: 64 records = 4 distinct SWE-Bench astropy instances (astropy__astropy-12907, -13033, -13236, -13398) x 16 samples each, 64 tokens each (4096 generated tokens). All length==64 (hit max_tokens), finish_reason=length.
- Acceptance ladder native_greedy: 4 records, 128 tokens each (512 tokens), one per prompt_id 0..3, and these ALSO carry prompt_token_ids (681/1080/829/1614 prompt tokens) so the per-request suffix tree can be seeded with the prompt. t06/seed1717 variants give 3 more 4x128 replicas.
- cat10 native_e5: 4 records, served_token_ids lens [128,128,86,51] = 393 tokens.
Total scored decode positions in the study = 4540 (68 requests: 64 deliverable + 4 ladder). Streams are SHORT (64-128 tok) — sufficient for a hit-rate distribution but they cap the uncapped-upside measurement and give a near-empty per-request tree early on.
data.globalCorpus: Usable cross-request GLOBAL corpus = the OTHER completed requests' served outputs. In the deliverable set this is rich: 64 completed SWE generations across 4 astropy tasks. For any target request the global tree was built from the other 63 (and, with the strict guard, only the ~48 from OTHER tasks). This is a legitimate cross-request corpus (other completed requests) with no self-future leakage. CAVEAT: the corpus is only 4 distinct SWE tasks, all astropy, sharing heavy agentic boilerplate ("I'll start by exploring the workspace..."), so the 16 same-task samples are near-duplicate siblings. I measured BOTH with same-task siblings in the global tree (the as-deployed agentic-repetition source, capped mean 2.293) and with a strict cross-task-only guard (capped mean 2.179) to bound the leakage. The per-request tree contributes almost nothing at these lengths (capped mean 0.099) — the entire suffix win comes from the GLOBAL tree.
data.contentType:
REAL SWE-Verified / code-agent generations (NOT toy/probe). Prompts are Codex-CLI SWE-Bench task invocations (astropy modeling separability_matrix bug fix etc.); outputs are agentic code-agent text: <think> blocks then "I'll start by exploring..." then bash/find commands and code — exactly SuffixDecoding's verbatim-echo sweet spot. token_ids are full vLLM output token-id streams from qwen3.6-27b (model field), mode naive_mtp = E5 native MTP-5 served. Content confirmed by detokenized text fields and instance_id SWE-Bench identifiers.

MEASURED RESULT (offline suffix-automaton, MAXP=8 match window, no GPU): suffix tail capped at depth 3 accepts a mean of 2.29 tokens (strict cross-task guard: 2.18), with the distribution heavily bimodal — 68.8% of positions reach the full 3-deep cap, 15.3% hit 0. Uncapped mean correct echo = 7.08 tokens (p90=16, the horizon cap), confirming long verbatim runs in the repetitive tail. Versus the cat9 deep nodes the suffix tail displaces (per-depth accept rates d3=0.483, d4=0.379, d5~0.30 -> sequential expected deep-tail accepts 0.721), the suffix tail wins by +1.57 (leaky/agentic-repeat) to +1.46 (strict cross-task) accepted tokens. On this banked data the load-bearing assumption HOLDS: the 3-deep model-free suffix tail accepts materially MORE than the displaced cat9 deep leaves. Hit-rate persists into the task-specific tail (gen[48:] still 1.79 capped, not pure boilerplate).
data.limitations:
Real, but caveat-heavy — do not over-read:
1. SCARCITY: only 4 distinct SWE prompts/tasks, all astropy, in the whole banked set. The 64-record richness is 16 near-duplicate samples per task, not corpus diversity. A production cross-request corpus would be far more varied; this set over-represents shared agentic boilerplate, which inflates the global-tree hit-rate. The strict cross-task number (2.18) is the more honest floor but is still only 4 tasks.
2. The ENTIRE suffix win comes from the GLOBAL cross-request tree (2.26); the PER-REQUEST online tree contributes ~0.10 at these lengths because streams are only 64-128 tokens (little self-repetition accrued yet). Longer agentic sessions would help the per-request tree, but that is unmeasured here.
3. Streams are SHORT (max 128 tok, mostly 64) -> uncapped upside is horizon-capped at 16 and the per-request tree never warms up; cannot measure long-session behavior.
4. This measures only the DRAFTER hit-rate (correctly-predicted continuation length). It does NOT include the GDN per-node verify tax (+2.9 ms/node on the replay route) or the cat10 dilution effect on co-resident accept/event — those need the GPU. The +1.46/+1.57 token margin is a NECESSARY but not SUFFICIENT condition for the net-TPS win; the per-node tax could still erode it.
5. Pick is an oracle best-of-(per-request, global) per position, mildly generous vs a single live tree, though global dominates so the effect is small.
6. NO future-token leakage in any number: per-request tree at position t contains only out[:t+1] (+prompt); the global tree contains only OTHER completed requests; guard verified by the near-zero per-request-only contribution (a leak would have inflated it). Reproduction scripts: /tmp/suffix_study.py and /tmp/suffix_study2.py (CPU-only, plain-Python suffix automaton).

replay.hitRates: Hit-rate = fraction of decode positions whose model-free suffix draft correctly predicts >=k of the actual served tokens (uncapped correct length). Measured on REAL banked SWE streams (no GPU, no leakage; verified). DELIVERABLE LEAKY / as-deployed (global tree includes same-task sibling samples, the real agentic-repetition source; n=4032 positions, 64 records): >=1 = 0.850, >=2 = 0.767, >=3 = 0.699. DELIVERABLE STRICT cross-task-only (global tree restricted to OTHER SWE tasks; bounds leakage; n=4032): >=1 = 0.718, >=2 = 0.628, >=3 = 0.554. LADDER prompt-seeded (4 records x128, per-request tree seeded with real prompt_token_ids 681/1080/829/1614; n=508): >=1 = 0.620, >=2 = 0.500, >=3 = 0.421. COMBINED leaky (deliverable+ladder, n=4540): >=1 = 0.839, >=2 = 0.752, >=3 = 0.683.
replay.correctLenDist: CORRECT_LEN distribution is heavily BIMODAL (the SuffixDecoding signature). DELIVERABLE LEAKY: capped-at-3 mean 2.317, median 3; uncapped mean 8.98, median 6, p90 22, max 51; frac_uncapped>=5 = 0.582, frac>=10 = 0.345. The capped distribution piles at the extremes: 69.9% reach the full 3-deep cap, 15.0% hit 0, leaving only ~15% in the middle. STRICT cross-task: capped mean 1.899, median 2; uncapped mean 5.35, median 3, p90 15, max 24; frac>=5 = 0.431; full-3 = 55.4%, zero = 28.2%. LADDER: capped mean 1.541; uncapped mean 3.59, p90 11, max 23; frac>=5 = 0.303. NOTE: streams are only 64-128 tokens so even the uncapped echo (max 51) is truncated by stream length, not by the MAX_DRAFT=64 horizon -- the true verbatim-echo ceiling is larger than measured. The long >=5 / >=10 echoes confirm the repetitive-tail win SuffixDecoding targets.
replay.expectedSuffixAcceptsAtTip: E[min(CORRECT_LEN,3)] = mean tokens the 3-deep model-free suffix tail accepts at the spine tip. DELIVERABLE LEAKY (as-deployed) = 2.317. DELIVERABLE STRICT cross-task = 1.899. LADDER prompt-seeded = 1.541. COMBINED leaky = 2.273. COMPARISON vs displaced cat9 deep nodes: cat9 per-depth accept rates d3=0.483/d4=0.379/d5~0.30 give a SEQUENTIAL expected deep-tail accept of 0.721 (d3 + d3*d4 + d3*d4*d5; you only reach d4 if d3 accepted). The suffix tail BEATS the displaced deep MTP nodes by +1.60 (leaky/as-deployed) to +1.18 (strict cross-task) accepted tokens. The load-bearing hybrid assumption HOLDS on this banked SWE data even under the strict cross-task leakage bound. Caveat: this is the per-tip accept gain, NOT a net TPS verdict -- it does not yet net out the GDN +2.9 ms/node replay tax or the cat10 dilution trap; a positive accept margin is necessary but not sufficient for the speed win.
replay.coldStartEffect: Essentially NO cold-start penalty for the suffix tail, because the win comes from the GLOBAL corpus (shared agentic boilerplate that opens every SWE generation -- "I'll start by exploring the workspace...") which is fully populated from token 0, masking any per-request-tree warmup. LEAKY capped mean by generation depth: gen 0-15 = 2.463, 16-31 = 2.402, 32-47 = 2.327, 48-63 = 2.057 -- STRONGEST early, gentle monotone decline (echo of boilerplate fades as generation becomes task-specific). Region split confirms: early first-quartile 2.471 vs mid/late 2.268 (leaky); strict 2.439 vs 1.731. The per-request tree contributes almost nothing at these short lengths (consistent with the data note's per-request capped mean ~0.099); the entire suffix win is carried by the global cross-request tree. This is the opposite of a classic per-request suffix cold start -- on repetitive agentic SWE the suffix tail is hot from t=0.
replay.perStreamSpread: Wide per-stream spread, confirming the win lives in the repetitive-echo tail of the distribution, not a uniform mean. DELIVERABLE LEAKY (64 streams): capped-mean per stream ranges min 1.127 to max 2.810, stdev 0.453. STRICT cross-task: min 1.032 to max 2.381, stdev 0.336. LADDER (4 streams): min 1.016 to max 1.764, stdev 0.305. Streams whose served output heavily re-echoes the shared boilerplate/code idioms hit ~2.8 (near the 3-cap), while more novel-prose streams sit near ~1.0 -- exactly the Spec-Bench-style spread (SuffixDecoding loses on novel prose, wins on verbatim echo). The mean (2.32) is therefore a blend; the deployed hybrid benefit will be concentrated in the high-repetition requests.

replay.summary: MEASURED OFFLINE (CPU-only, plain-Python suffix-automaton over MAXP=8 match windows; no GPU/model/container; arctic-inference not importable so a longest-match context->max-frequency-continuation lookup was used, sufficient for hit-rate). Data = REAL banked SWE-Verified served streams: 64 deliverable records (4 astropy SWE tasks x16 temp0.6 samples, 64 tok each, native MTP-5 / mode=naive_mtp) + 4 acceptance-ladder records (128 tok, WITH real prompt_token_ids to seed the per-request tree). 4540 scored decode positions. NO-LEAKAGE: per-request tree is strictly causal (only prompt + x_{<=t}); global tree never contains the target's own tokens; an adversarial self-test that replaces the target's future with random tokens collapses the capped hit-rate to exactly 0.0 (passed) -- proving no future-token peeking. VERDICT: the load-bearing hybrid assumption HOLDS on this banked data. The 3-deep model-free suffix tail accepts E[min(CL,3)] = 2.317 tokens as-deployed (1.899 under the strict cross-task leakage bound) at the spine tip, vs only 0.721 sequential-expected accepts from the cat9 deep MTP nodes (d3-d5) it displaces -- a margin of +1.60 (leaky) to +1.18 (strict). Distribution is bimodal (69.9% hit the full 3-cap, 15.0% hit 0; uncapped echo mean 8.98, p90 22, max 51 = long verbatim runs in the repetitive tail). No cold-start penalty (global boilerplate carries it from t=0). CAVEATS: (1) banked streams are SHORT (64-128 tok), so the per-request tree is near-empty early and the uncapped upside is truncated by stream length; (2) corpus is only 4 astropy tasks with heavy shared boilerplate, so leaky and strict bound the true leakage; (3) this measures the per-tip ACCEPT gain ONLY -- it does NOT net out the GDN +2.9 ms/node replay tax or the cat10 +1-row dilution trap, so a positive accept margin is necessary-but-not-sufficient for the TPS win, which still needs a live GPU measurement. Within those limits the offline evidence supports proceeding to a GPU slot.

verdict.expectedSuffixAccepts: A = E[min(CORRECT_LEN,3)] = mean tokens the 3-deep model-free suffix tail accepts at the spine tip, from the no-leakage replay over 4540 real banked SWE decode positions: 2.317 leaky/as-deployed (deliverable, same-task siblings in global tree = the real agentic-repetition source), 1.899 under the STRICT cross-task-only leakage bound, 2.273 combined leaky, 1.541 prompt-seeded ladder (cold-corpus proxy, per-request tree only). Distribution is bimodal (SuffixDecoding signature): 69.9% reach the full 3-cap, 15.0% hit 0; uncapped echo mean 8.98, p90 22, max 51. Adversarial self-test (replace target future with random tokens) collapses capped mean to exactly 0.0 = no future-token leakage confirmed.
verdict.displacedCat9Accepts: B = 0.721 tokens. The 3-deep suffix tail displaces cat9's DEEP MTP tail (d3-d5 spine). Using cat9 per-depth accept RATES (FR13_CAT10_BIND.md:61) d3=0.483, d4=0.379, d5~0.30, the sequential-expected yield of that deep tail (you only reach d4 if d3 accepted, d5 if d4 accepted) = 0.483 + 0.483*0.379 + 0.483*0.379*0.30 = 0.721. That is roughly what those ~3 displaced verify rows contribute today.
verdict.taxNodes: 3 nodes. The 3-deep tail pays the GDN per-node replay tax (+2.9 ms/node, replay route; legacy +42-46 ms/node) on EVERY forward, even on a suffix miss. CRITICAL: the tail SWAPS the cat9 deep spine rows (d3-d5), which already carry the same GDN node traffic and lm-head rows today, so the 3-node tax is NOT net-new for a like-for-like row swap; net-new node count is ~0. This contrasts with cat10, which ADDED a 4th co-resident row (10 vs 9) for +2.9 ms/fwd that was not offset.
verdict.breakEven: Margin A - B: +1.60 (leaky/as-deployed), +1.18 (strict cross-task bound), +1.55 (combined), +0.82 (cold-corpus ladder). Because the tail is a pure SWAP of deep rows (net-new node count ~0), the break-even threshold in accept-token terms is essentially A - B > 0, which holds in EVERY variant including the strict leakage bound and even the cold-corpus ladder. To dip below break-even the suffix tail would have to drop from the measured 1.90-2.32 down to B=0.721 accepts (a 2.6-3.2x degradation) AND incur a net-new node beyond the swap. Equivalently: if a non-swap variant added the tail on top of the existing rows, the +2.9 ms/node would cost ~1 lm-head-row-equivalent (~2.9 ms/row), still covered by the +1.18 to +1.60 token margin. Cat10's -0.27 dilution does not recur here because the tail adds no d0-d2 co-resident drafter row.
verdict.conditions: GO to a single GPU prototype arm (n=2, 3-deep tip tail, replay route, GLOBAL corpus warm), CONDITIONAL on: (1) GLOBAL-CORPUS WARM IS REQUIRED - the entire win is carried by the cross-request global tree (shared agentic boilerplate, hot from t=0); the per-request tree contributes ~0.099 capped mean at these short lengths. Deploy with the global tree populated; a per-request-only / cold-corpus arm is the thin-margin worst case (+0.82). (2) The arm must be a pure SWAP of the cat9 deep spine (d3-d5) for the suffix tail, NOT an additive +1 row - additive is the cat10 -0.27 trap. (3) WINS ARE WORKLOAD-CONCENTRATED in the high-repetition / verbatim-echo tail: per-stream capped mean ranges 1.13-2.81 (leaky), so the benefit is concentrated in echo-heavy SWE requests; novel-prose-heavy requests (~1.0-1.3) barely beat B - the deployed gain is a blend, not uniform. (4) The GPU arm must net out two things this CPU study did NOT measure: the live GDN +2.9 ms/node replay tax on real co-residency and whether the tail re-triggers any d1-d4 dilution at B=2-4; a positive accept margin is necessary but not sufficient for the TPS verdict. (5) Lossless gate (per-token argmax + within-floor) must still pass on the live arm - the suffix tail is model-free so it must be verified, never trusted.
verdict.summary: The single load-bearing hybrid assumption HOLDS on real banked SWE data. The 3-deep model-free suffix tail accepts E[min(CL,3)] = 2.317 tokens as-deployed (1.899 under the strict cross-task leakage bound) at the spine tip, vs only 0.721 sequential-expected accepts from the cat9 deep MTP nodes (d3-d5) it displaces = a margin of +1.60 (leaky) to +1.18 (strict), positive even cold (+0.82 ladder). Because the tail SWAPS deep rows rather than adding one, the +2.9 ms/node GDN tax is ~net-zero node count, so break-even is A-B>0, cleared in every variant; and it avoids cat10's -0.27 dilution (which came from an ADDED co-resident row, not a swap). Measurement is sound: causal no-leakage suffix automaton, adversarial random-future self-test collapses to 0.0, 4540 real SWE decode positions, CPU-only. CAVEATS: (1) banked streams are short (64-128 tok) so the per-request tree is near-empty and uncapped echo (max 51) is truncated by stream length, not the draft horizon; (2) corpus is only 4 astropy tasks with heavy shared boilerplate - leaky and strict bracket the true leakage; (3) the win is bimodal and concentrated in the high-repetition echo tail, not uniform; (4) this is the per-tip ACCEPT gain ONLY and does NOT net out the live GDN replay tax or B=2-4 co-residency dilution - a GPU measurement is still required. Within those limits the offline evidence supports spending one GPU slot. VERDICT: CONDITIONAL-GO with a global-corpus-warm, deep-row-SWAP arm. redteam.noLeakage: CLEAN — no future-token leakage. The script's causal guard is correct: at each position t it sets future=out[t+1:], appends out[t] to history, and indexes only contexts that END strictly before the newly-emitted token (lo=max(0,prev_len-MAXP)..prev_len), with an explicit assert len(history)==len(prompt)+t+1. build_global skips the target index entirely. I confirmed this with THREE independent tests, not just the banked self-test: (1) the incremental per-request index at every t exactly equals a fresh-from-scratch rebuild of SuffixIndex(prompt+out[:t+1]) for all 64 streams (0 mismatches) — proves no future bleed; (2) corrupting the future tokens collapses capped-mean to EXACTLY 0.0 for ALL 64 streams (the banked leakage_selftest only checked stream 0 -> 2.222 baseline / 0.0 corrupted; I extended it to all 64, all collapse); (3) the leaky global index provably matches an other-streams-only rebuild and never contains the target's own pairs. No off-by-one. The draft is a pure function of history[:t+1] plus other completed requests.
redteam.fairComparison: STRUCTURALLY FAIR with one honest, non-fatal asymmetry. A=E[min(CL,3)] scores the 3-token continuation immediately AFTER position t (the post-tip window x_{t+1..t+3}); B=0.721 scores cat9's same d3-d5 deep window. The retained MTP head (d0-d2, rates 0.871/0.828/0.638) is identical in both arms and CANCELS, so there is NO double-counting — it is a clean tail-vs-tail swap. B's arithmetic reproduces exactly: 0.483 + 0.483*0.379 + 0.483*0.379*0.30 = 0.721 (sequential, correctly conditioned on reaching each depth). The one asymmetry: A is measured unconditionally at every position while B is conditioned on the spine surviving to d3; the hybrid tail only fires when the spine reaches the tip. But this is non-fatal — even the WORST single stream (capped-mean 1.127 leaky / 1.032 strict) beats B=0.721, so the margin survives the harshest conditioning sensitivity. Margins reproduce: +1.60 leaky / +1.18 strict / +0.82 ladder.
redteam.dataSufficient: MARGINAL — this is the binding weakness and the reason the verdict must stay CONDITIONAL, not GO. 4032 positions sounds large but there are only 4 INDEPENDENT prompts, ALL astropy, 16 temp-varied samples each. Effective N for cross-task generalization is ~4, not 4032 (positions are heavily autocorrelated). The leaky variant feeds 15 near-identical same-task siblings into the global tree (worth ~0.418 of A, 18%); the strict cross-task variant still shares astropy import/boilerplate so it is NOT a true held-out task and likely overstates a genuinely novel SWE instance. Streams are only 64-128 tokens, so the per-request tree is near-empty (capped mean ~0.099) and the uncapped echo (max 51) is truncated by stream length not the draft horizon — the entire win is carried by the global corpus. The margin is ROBUST in direction (positive in every variant incl. the cold per-request-only ladder +0.82), but the absolute magnitude is corpus-optimistic. A wider/more-diverse SWE corpus is needed before any GO.
redteam.beatsCat10Dilution: YES, with comfortable headroom. The cat10 trap was -0.27 accept/event from ADDING a 4th co-resident d0 row. The suffix margin A-B is +1.18 (strict) to +1.60 (leaky) = 4.4x-5.9x the dilution magnitude; even if the live GPU arm re-incurs a full cat10-style -0.27, the +1.18 token margin absorbs it with ~+0.91 to spare. Structurally the tail is a SWAP of cat9's existing d3-d5 deep spine rows (net-new node count ~0), not an ADD, so the +2.9 ms/node GDN tax is not net-new and the dilution mechanism (extra co-resident drafter row) need not recur. The break-even reduces to A-B>0, cleared in every variant including the cold ladder.
redteam.trustworthyVerdict: CONDITIONAL-GO to a single GPU prototype arm. The load-bearing hybrid assumption HOLDS: the 3-deep model-free suffix tail accepts E[min(CL,3)]=1.90 (strict cross-task bound) to 2.32 (as-deployed leaky) tokens at the spine tip vs only 0.721 sequential-expected from the cat9 d3-d5 deep MTP it displaces = +1.18 to +1.60 margin, positive even cold (+0.82). The measurement is methodologically sound (reproduces exactly on re-run; causal no-leakage suffix automaton verified 3 ways; bimodal SuffixDecoding signature present: 69.9% reach the 3-cap, frac_uncapped>=5 = 0.58). The CONDITIONAL (not GO) is driven entirely by the thin/correlated corpus (4 astropy tasks) — the margin direction is robust but its magnitude needs a more diverse SWE corpus. The SINGLE thing the GPU prototype must measure that this CPU study cannot: the LIVE GDN +2.9 ms/node replay tax under real co-residency AND whether the tail re-triggers d1-d4 dilution at B=2-4 (i.e., the net TPS / accept-per-event verdict). A positive offline accept margin is necessary but not sufficient for the speed win; and the model-free tail must still clear the per-token-argmax + within-floor lossless gate (verified, never trusted).
redteam.issues: No material flaw invalidates the study; all headline numbers reproduce exactly and leakage is provably absent (3 independent tests). Remaining caveats, none fatal: (1) DATA THINNESS is the real limiter — only 4 independent astropy prompts; 'strict cross-task' still shares astropy boilerplate so it is an upper-leaning bound on a truly novel task, and the leaky variant's 15 same-task siblings contribute ~18% of A. Effective task-level N=4, not 4032 positions. (2) Short 64-128 tok streams mean the per-request tree contributes ~nothing and the uncapped echo is stream-length-truncated — the win rides entirely on the global corpus, so global-warm is a hard precondition (cold-boot/per-request-only is the +0.82 worst case). (3) A is measured unconditionally while B is conditioned on spine-survival-to-d3; mitigated because even the worst single stream (1.03-1.13) still beats B. (4) The study is correctly scoped as a per-tip ACCEPT-margin measurement, NOT a TPS verdict — it does not net out the live GDN tax or B>1 co-residency dilution; that gap is exactly why the verdict is CONDITIONAL and is the GPU arm's job. (5) Verdict survives the cat10 precedent by 4-6x and the SWAP-not-ADD structure avoids the dilution mechanism, but that swap is an assumption about the live topology only the GPU arm can confirm.
